No content application. It also polls its hub inbox outbound-only, storing deliveries durably before acknowledging; received observations are never applied. M3 step 3: the `wp.service` domain reports a coverage projection (`collection.order` under profile `wp-service-inventory-v1`, the sorted set of portable UIDs; complete only when every observed post has a UID) on reconciliation and after every per-object change, so the hub can verify absence for service posts; the Add-ons tab shows a read-only inbox table. Slice A1 ships the shell, Overview (hub stat cards + attention list, connector connection/coverage/pending cards), Settings (gates, apply confirmation, enrollment/resume) and the Run now runners; the page never prints tokens or app passwords. records.title: Agency Control hub: enrollment, receipt, routing, inbox, comparison, framework review, releases, preparation and approval
records.summary: Independently gated studio-hub add-on. Enabling it installs hub stores and registers dbvc-agency/v1 enrollment exchange, observation receipt, capabilities, inbox and inbox/ack routes. Enrolled environments authenticate with a bound WordPress application password; the hub assigns the epoch, stores immutable events with per-event outcomes, routes each accepted event through the trusted registry (explicit client and framework subscriptions) into per-target deliveries with a frozen policy revision and into raw framework review items, keeps sequence-guarded projections, and holds enrollments on site-URL drift. No comparison, promotion or content application. M3 step 1 adds hash-level three-way environment comparison over each environment's own projections and explicitly confirmed pair/object baselines (with operator instance links for independently enrolled lineages). M3 step 2 adds immutable framework definition versions (studio-supplied order, per-channel desired version), explicit adoption on framework subscriptions, approved overrides (exact hash, frozen policy revision, rationale; needs_rebase_review when the desired version changes) and a read-only framework status report; nothing applies content or promotes a client edit. M3 step 3 adds review-item resolution through the status report (`observed → classified → resolved`, automatic for superseded/clean/approved-and-current items, explicit with a note otherwise) and an administrator panel in DBVC's Add-ons tab (environments, open invitations, framework status, review items, and an invitation form whose token is shown once via admin-post + a per-user transient; the action registers only inside wp-admin). M4 step 1 adds release manifests (objects selected from a source environment's current projections with fixed after-hashes), authorized payload transfer (the source connector supplies canonical bodies that the hub verifies by hash before the release seals with a digest), per-target prepare requests and immutable prepare receipts (the target connector's dry run, stored with its digest and annotated with the hub's own projections/baselines). Machine routes: GET releases/payload-requests, POST releases/{uid}/payloads, GET releases/prepare-requests, POST releases/{uid}/prepare-receipts. Nothing applies content; a receipt expires and is not permission to write. M4 step 2: release items carry an operation (replace, or delete for a verified absence whose payload is the canonical null); the administrator panel lists releases and prepare receipts. M5 step 1 adds approvals (dbvc_ac_approvals): an explicit studio action on a received ready/no-op prepare receipt that binds release digest, receipt digest, target epoch and policy revision, expires with the receipt, is retrieved by the target on its own poll (GET releases/apply-requests), and is consumed by exactly one execution receipt (POST releases/{uid}/apply-receipts); verified applied objects advance the pair baseline.

surfaces.identifier: DBVC_Agency_Control_Addon gate and settings owner; Dbvc\AgencyControl\Runtime::boot()

Hub-owned stores (created only through the enable lifecycle)

requirements: dbvc_addon_agency_control_enabled = '1' (off by default) and DBVC_AGENCY_EMERGENCY_DISABLE undefined or false
Application passwords available (HTTPS, or WP_ENVIRONMENT_TYPE=local for disposable labs)
inputs: Administrator invitation requests (wp dbvc agency invite)
Connector exchange requests carrying a single-use token
outputs: Service user + application password per environment (credential returned once in the exchange response)
Environment registry rows with hub-assigned epoch and status enabled|held|revoked
Immutable received events with routing_state=pending and per-event outcomes
Sequence-guarded projections and gap summaries
Per-target deliveries (delivery_id doubles as the target's inbox cursor; pending survive offline targets; cancelled at retrieval when a subscription is disabled or the source revoked)
Framework review items in state observed (raw observations awaiting the M3 adopted-version comparison)
Three-way comparison rows (synchronized|outgoing|incoming|converged|conflict|baseline_required|unknown with reasons, observed flags, hashes) and confirmed baselines

warnings: Writes are management data only: users, application passwords, invitations, environments, events, projections. No site content is ever modified.
Only the SHA-256 of an invitation token is stored; the token and the application password are shown exactly once.
Machine routes accept only the enrolled application-password principal; administrator cookies and unbound application passwords are refused (401/403).
Observation bodies carry no recipients, client or agency fields; such fields are rejected per event. A sender-labelled apply origin is stored as an ordinary observation.
ACK means durable receipt, not delivery; routing/delivery are not implemented (routing_state stays pending).
Routing reads membership only from the registry; wire fields naming recipients, clients or agencies are rejected; a sender-labelled apply origin never suppresses framework review.
Inbox retrieval serves only the authenticated target's pending deliveries and rechecks subscription/source status; acknowledgements affect only that target's ids.

Baselines advance only through wp dbvc agency baseline-confirm (equal, complete, fresh projections; --accept-absent for one-sided verified absence); receipt, routing, delivery and acknowledgement never touch them. Comparison is hash-level: it classifies, it cannot show path diffs.

known_gaps: Framework adopted versions, approved overrides and definition catalog (M3 step 2) are not implemented; review items stay `observed`. wp.service never-observed target objects stay unknown because the domain has no collection-coverage projection. Independently created (not DBVC-imported) posts differ by post_date_gmt.
Site-URL hold compares the sender header with the enrolled URL; an identical clone (same URL) is indistinguishable until it re-enrolls.
Live verification ran in a disposable three-server lab loading this checkout, not on the active LocalWP site.

opportunity.rationale: Delivery/inbox routes and subscriptions follow in the next reporting step once receipt is reviewed.

records.title: Agency Control invite, subscription, routing, baseline, framework and hold/release/revoke commands
records.summary: wp dbvc agency invite creates a single-use expiring enrollment invitation (token printed once); subscribe / subscribe-framework / unsubscribe / enable-subscription manage explicit same-client subscriptions and framework bindings; route processes pending received events into deliveries and review items; baseline-confirm records pair/object baselines for currently agreeing objects (--accept-absent for one-sided verified absence); link-instance / unlink-instance declare lineage between instances on two environments; revoke deletes the environment's application password; release clears a hold after review. definition-publish records an immutable definition version (hash supplied, read from one environment's fresh complete projection, or copied from a published version; order explicit or by publish sequence, never inferred from the label) and definition-desire marks a channel's desired version (approved overrides on that channel become needs_rebase_review); adopt-version declares which version a framework subscription follows; override-approve records an exact approved hash with rationale and the frozen policy revision; override-detach ends it. review-classify stamps open review items with the drift/version state from framework-status (auto-resolving superseded, clean/current and approved-and-current items) and review-resolve closes one explicitly with a note. release-create fixes an immutable manifest from a source environment's current projections (payloads are then collected from its connector and verified by hash), release-withdraw ends one, prepare-request asks a target to dry-run a sealed release (its connector returns the receipt; nothing is written). approve binds a received ready/no-op prepare receipt for execution; revoke-approval withdraws an unconsumed approval. `hold --environment --reason` places an operator hold (recorded as operator:<note>): the hub refuses the environment's batches with 409 and keeps its deliveries pending until `release`; revoked environments cannot be held. `rollback --operation` creates a reviewed rollback (an approval-like record with kind=rollback bound to a consumed operation's execution digest); the target restores its journalled before image on its next poll with one conditional write per container guarded by the operation's after fingerprint (a container that moved on yields a restore conflict, never an overwrite), and the hub regresses the pair baseline to the restored hash.
outputs: invite: invitation id, token (once), expiry, hub URL
revoke/release: resulting environment status

warnings: The invitation token is authority to enroll one environment until it expires; transmit it out of band and never commit it.
Revocation is terminal for that enrollment; the environment must re-enroll with a new invitation.
Subscriptions are validated against the registry (same agency and client, both enrolled, no self-subscription); disabling one cancels its pending deliveries at the target's next retrieval.
Definition versions are immutable once published; a new desired version never rewrites or removes an override, it only flags it for rebase review. No command here writes content to any environment.

approve authorizes the target connector to write one release (Bricks global classes/variables) on its next poll, only while its own apply gate is on and only against the container fingerprints its receipt recorded; the approval expires with the receipt and is consumed by one execution receipt.

known_gaps: No administrator UI for invitations yet.

opportunity.rationale: Hub administration screens belong with the review/inbox step.
